method: Primary official pages and query responses reread using the research fetch tool on 2026-10-22. This claim ledger is not a byte-authenticated copy of remote sites; shell HTTP reachability failures are recorded separately.

verified_claims: The task is fault mapping, not direct verification of geothermal vents or productive reservoirs.
Experts labeled faults absent from the public USGS catalogue for testing; final-round labels will also include expert-reviewed discoveries.
The metric uses alpha 0.2, beta 0.8 and a triangular kernel with 300 m support.
The required output is one float32 prediction band with values in [0,1], EPSG:32611, 100 m resolution and matching bounds.
The format paragraph says data outside the bounds is null or nan; local all-finite zero fill is a project convention, not proof of portal acceptance.

The provided-feature list names surface conductivity and depth to conductive base surface. The owner-mirrored band 15 tag instead describes sedimentary basement depth; the meanings must not be assumed equivalent.
limits: No access to private labels, authenticated account capacity, or artifact-linked organizer receipts.

sources.authority: DOE / National Laboratory of the Rockies, September 2026 official rules
sources.access: Title and sections 3.1 through 3.6 read successfully
verified_claims: Section 3.2 permits generative AI with narrative disclosure and makes the competitor responsible for accuracy and authenticity.
Sections 3.2 and 3.4 specify up to three scoring submissions per week.
Section 3.4 allows one finalized submission per participating entity and prohibits a team member from submitting a separate final entry.
Finalists must provide code and documentation sufficient to reproduce the solution.
limits: The rules' weekly maximum is not a measurement of remaining account slots.

verified_claims: Airborne magnetics and radiometrics support subsurface and surface geological interpretation, respectively.
Area 1 flight-line spacing is 200 m; Area 2 spacing is 400 m; both use flight-line azimuth 90 degrees.
Actual terrain clearance varies with aircraft climb/descent limitations and should be considered during interpretation.
The release includes magnetic and radiometric grids, flight-line CSV data and flight-path shapefiles.
The USGS page marks the release CC0 1.0 Universal.
limits: No new original flight-line binary was downloaded in this session; existing uint8 derivatives are not calibrated concentration measurements.

sources.access: Resource listing and license read successfully
verified_claims: The regional compilation lists shallow temperature probes, magnetics, gravity, geodetics, conductance, paleogeothermal features, volcanic features, wells and springs.
The landing page states public access and CC BY 4.0; redistribution requires attribution.
The linked MT resource describes conductance integrated over depth ranges, not sub-kilometre resistivity slices.
limits: Mirrored derived files were hash-restored separately. This page does not independently authenticate those derivatives or their column transformations.

sources.access: Official release description and file listing read successfully via DOI redirect
verified_claims: Electrical conductance is the integration of electrical conductivity over a depth range.
gb_conductance_surface_tp.tif integrates 2–12 km depth; the other four ranges extend from 12 to 200 km.
This listed product does not provide the 500 m and 1500 m resistivity slices asserted by the previous H80-MT-PHASE plan.
limits: A new source or reconstruction with justified resolution would be needed for that shallow-slice hypothesis. Metadata access is not successful binary acquisition.

sources.access: ScienceBase metadata and item JSON read; public downloadUri and file metadata listed
verified_claims: Background conductive heat-flow maps deliberately de-emphasize convectively influenced outliers using iterative weighted LOESS.
The release also provides well-point residuals; the authors say these may help identify hydrothermal or groundwater influence.
ScienceBase JSON exposes a public downloadUri for the supporting-data ZIP (130,154,244 listed bytes, about 124.12 MiB); no archive bytes were transferred.
limits: The listed ZIP bytes and advertised MD5 were not downloaded or locally verified. Coordinate/field coverage, file-level reuse terms, and residual QA remain unverified; the residual hypothesis is still blocked by preflight and not execution-ready.

verified_claims: Database compiles Quaternary faults demonstrating geological evidence of coseismic surface deformation in M>6 earthquakes, and notes hazard-map traces are simplified geometry representations.
Public-domain GIS archive URL: https://earthquake.usgs.gov/static/lfs/nshm/qfaults/Qfaults_GIS.zip.
limits: Explains catalogue omission of sub-M6 accommodation faults, alluvial/playa-buried blind geothermal feeders, and simplified outboard piedmont splays.
